name: colophon
description: Turns markdown into typeset PDF documentation - cover page, contents, diagrams and glossary - using the AI already in your editor. No Docker, no database, no API key.
author: Mohamed Yassine Reggui

commands.title: Colophon: Discover Models for Custom Provider
Colophon: Open Settings in VS Code

colophon.convertOnSave.description: Convert a markdown file to PDF when it is saved.

colophon.enrich.description: Use the editor's language model to add a summary, glossary and diagrams. Every claim is checked against your document before it is printed; unsupported ones are dropped.

colophon.debounceMs.description: How long to wait after a save before converting.

colophon.autoProcess.description: Process a markdown file when it is saved. Per-project automation is set from the dashboard's Auto transform switch; this is the global gate.

colophon.includePatterns.description: Glob patterns for files to include in auto-processing.

colophon.excludePatterns.description: Glob patterns to skip. Tool-generated scaffolding is excluded by default.

colophon.maxConcurrentProcessing.description: Maximum number of files converted at once.

colophon.allowRuleBasedFallback.description: Produce a plain PDF when no AI provider is available, instead of reporting an error. Off by default so missing AI is noticed rather than silently producing a document with no glossary or diagrams.

colophon.enableDebugLogging.description: Verbose logging in the Speckit output channel.

colophon.preferredModelId.description: Substring matched case-insensitively against the id, family or name of the available models, e.g. "gpt-4o". If it matches, that model is tried first.

colophon.providerPriority.description: Order in which AI providers are tried. Use custom:<id> to name one entry from colophon.customModels.

colophon.customModels.markdownDescription:
### ➜ [Manage AI providers](command:colophon.manageProviders)

OpenAI-compatible endpoints of your own - a local Ollama, a company gateway. VS Code cannot render an array-of-objects setting, so this row only offers raw JSON; the panel writes it for you, and also tests an endpoint and lists the models it actually serves.

name.description: Display name, shown in logs and in the try order.

baseUrl.description: Up to but not including /chat/completions, e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1

modelName.description: Exactly as the endpoint expects it - an id from its own /models listing.

models.description: Whatever the last discovery run returned, so the model picker has something to show without going back to the network.

endpoint.description: Legacy: a full chat-completions URL written by an earlier build. Still read, and folded onto baseUrl the next time this entry is saved.

model.description: Legacy: replaced by modelName. Still read.

label.description: Legacy: replaced by name. Still read.

scripts.build: npm run compile && npm run build:webview
scripts.package: npm run build && vsce package --target win32-x64
